cells.tense: The practice is finished for today, and you are still in it, feeling it settle.
cells.ask: Before you stand up, sit one minute longer and name to yourself which part of the session actually landed — then close the book and go.
cells.core: You know when a thing is done, and you can feel it being done. Most people can do one or the other. You sit down, you put in the reps, and when the session ends you let it end — you don't drag the last set out trying to squeeze more, and you don't walk away before you've felt what it gave you.\n\nThat's the whole thing working. The small daily practice you keep isn't just producing skill; it's giving the feeling somewhere quiet to land, and you're letting it land. Tonight the habit is to keep the door open. When someone asks what it's for, say the true thing instead of the modest one.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish a thing and feel it finished at the same time.
cells.verb: letting something be finished and felt as finished
cells.place: in the small daily practice that no one watches

cells.tense: You will be finished with this before you have actually done it, and you are already rehearsing the ending.
cells.ask: Pick the one next step in front of you and do only that — then stop, even if there is more in you, and write one line about how it felt.
cells.core: You're running ahead of the thing again. Somewhere ahead of you is the version where the practice is complete, the skill is built, the feeling is all settled — and you're living in that version instead of this afternoon's reps. So you push past the point where the work was good and turn it into catching up with a finish line that isn't there yet.\n\nThe cost is that nothing gets to land. This is supposed to be slow built skill; you're asking it to hand you a whole at once. Let one step be the step. Then let the pause be real too — that's the part you keep skipping, and it's the part that brings the feeling home.
cells.sheetLine: You keep finishing things before you've done them.

cells.tense: The practice is not happening, and the part of today that would end well is not arriving either.
cells.ask: Do the smallest version of the practice today, badly, for five minutes — no plan for what it builds toward — and notice one thing about it as you stop.
cells.core: The practice isn't happening. You can see the chair from here and you're not in it. Days end without the one small thing that used to close them, and the settled feeling that came with finishing a session has nowhere to land — so evenings just stop rather than finish.\n\nYou're not short on feeling. You're short on the doorway it used to come through, and standing outside it makes starting the next one harder each time. You don't have to care about the practice to do it. Five minutes, no goal, is enough to make today real. Whatever comes up while you do it is what today gets to be about.
cells.sheetLine: The practice stopped, and the day doesn't close without it.
cells.verb: letting something be finished and felt as finished

cells.tense: You are ending things well and telling yourself it is just how the week went.
cells.ask: Name one thing you actually finished this week and say out loud what it took — to yourself, or to someone who was there.
cells.core:
You're already closing things properly. Projects get wrapped, doors get shut, and the feeling that comes with a clean ending shows up on schedule — you just file it as being organized. Somebody notices how you land a thing. You call it keeping up.

That's not modesty, it's a blind spot. The finishing keeps happening and the feeling keeps getting dismissed, so you don't get to know your own pattern or trust it the next time something ends. Nothing new to build here. Just start counting what's already yours.

You've been doing the whole move the entire time. The only thing missing is your name on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already finishing well and calling it nothing.
cells.verb: letting something be finished and felt as finished

The four cells read as one capacity: letting a thing be finished and felt — Too Much forces the ending early, Too Little never lets the last page turn, Unacknowledged is already doing it and calling it nothing.
